Cincinnati Western Viaduct 3D

Cincinnati Western Viaduct

The two-level viaduct across Millvale, from the north trunk to the western hillside tunnels, at real size on the Deck's tracks and streets. The lower deck went up with Union Terminal in 1930 to 1933, four tracks wide, with a flat junction on the Western Hills line’s 1913 to 1920 masonry viaduct and its piers made to carry a second deck later. The upper deck came in the APEx era, on portal frames standing on the old pillars; after the Beekman Street arch APEx and RER D split, RER D into the old Cincinnati Western tunnel and APEx into a new high-speed tunnel beside it.

Tracks, streets, the culvert and ground are the Deck's (published layout in the hub repo) and the map 3 ground; Millvale is finished flat at about 151.5 m, and every footing goes down below the fill (Ben, 28 October). Levels follow Ben's option B (28 October): the Western Hills line at 162 m at the crossing, the upper rail at 174.8 m. The 1933 junction follows Ben's sketch: the south pair crosses the Western Hills line on the flat to the Cincinnati Western tunnel; the north pair turns north on one curve as the Cumminsville Spur into the east half of the Western Hills viaduct, which is four tracks wide north of the spur, and runs on west, built but without rails, as far as the arch beyond the Western Hills line, where the four tracks end (the second tunnel approach was to be its own structure); from there the 1933 deck is the two-track approach to the existing tunnel; the two seldom-used curves link the Western Hills line to CUT and to the tunnel. Today the crossing, the curves' tracks and the deck west of the Western Hills line are gone; the curve to the tunnel stands as a stub, and the old four-track deck is South Cumminsville, three tracks with side platforms (R5 on the centre track).

The streets are Ben's live Deck layout. The viaduct crosses the street grid at about 45°, so its pillars are bents skewed to run parallel to the street beside them, about 25 m apart (Ben, 29 October), with plate girders between; no column stands in a street and nothing reaches past the deck. Millvale Boulevard and its confluence park, over the culvert, carry nothing: the 1933 two-rib steel half-through arch clears them, its ribs springing from the end pillars above the ground, with the thrust carried down through them. The Beekman Street arch west of the Western Hills line stays; the four tracks end at it. The spans that meet the Western Hills viaduct are girders. Today Ben's portal frames stand only at the pillars, on the pillars' 1930s stubs and skewed with them, and hang the lower catenary; steel girders under the upper slab carry it from frame to frame, and two steel tied arches cross the junction where frames cannot stand (where R5 leaves the band and over RER A). Over the steel arch the upper deck rests on cross beams on posts on the ribs.

Drawing values: columns 1.4 m square, bents 1.6 m, the arch's end columns 3.0 by 2.4 m, arch abutments 5.0 m, girders span ÷ 10 deep at mid-span and span ÷ 7 at the bents (the railway plate-girder range), the steel ribs 2.4 m deep, springing as low as the streets under them allow, with their tops 0.5 m under the upper deck's structure, hangers and floor beams at 6 m, cross beams 2.85 m deep, frame haunches 2.4 m, the lower contact wire and messenger 5.3 and 5.8 m over the rail, the upper deck 1.9 m from rail to soffit, platforms 1.0 m over the rail, APEx-era portals at about 30 m, steel girders under the upper slab span ÷ 10 deep, the tied arches' rise span ÷ 6.5.
